 AFCON Qualifier: Aba fans urge Super Eagles to triumph over Tanzania
 Fri, Nov 13, 2026 
 By editor 
 2 MIN READ 
 Sports 
 SOME football fans in Aba have urged the Super Eagles to improve their performance and display better teamwork ahead of their 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) qualifying match against Tanzania on Friday.
 The fans made the call in separate interviews with the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) in Aba on Wednesday.
 They said the players needed to demonstrate greater commitment, discipline and tactical awareness to secure victory against their Tanzanian opponents.
 NAN reports that Nigeria won its opening qualifying match 2-1 against Madagascar before suffering a 0-3 defeat to Guinea-Bissau in the second match.
 A football enthusiast, Amarachi Uguru, urged the players to work together, adhere to the technical crew’s instructions and maintain a solid defence and effective attack.
 She said the performance gap between the Super Eagles and other African teams was narrowing, adding that Nigeria needed to reclaim its position among the continent’s leading football nations.
 “We missed the last World Cup, and Nigerians will not accept any excuse for failing to qualify for the Nations Cup,” she said.
 Similarly, Angela Okete, a student and football enthusiast, said she was initially excited by Nigeria’s 2-1 victory over Madagascar but disappointed by the subsequent 0-3 defeat to Guinea-Bissau.
 She expressed confidence in the experience of the Super Eagles players but urged them to demonstrate greater physical strength and determination.
 “Super Eagles have experienced players to overcome Tanzania, but our players need to bring out the physical aspect of their game.
 “The players also need to be focused for the 90 minutes duration of the game and avoid unnecessary errors at this stage,” Okete said.
 A grassroots footballer, Chidera Mba, urged the team to score early goals to put pressure on their opponents and secure a convincing victory.
 He said scoring early would also help Nigeria improve its position in the qualifying group and avoid depending on last-minute calculations.
 Similarly, Chimobi Madukwe called on the Super Eagles’ technical crew to field experienced players capable of matching Tanzania’s strength.
 “This is not the time to look down on any team but time to do the work on the field of play because our position is not encouraging,” he said.
 NAN reports that Nigeria occupy second position in Group L of the AFCON qualifiers with three points, behind Guinea-Bissau, who have six points.( NAN )
